title: La Paire
logline: Three weeks from retirement, a night-shift supermarket cashier with one hour on a parking meter tails a 'pickpocket pair' through the rooms of a Fès hammam, until the woman she has watched only from behind starts to turn, and she looks at the clock instead and leaves.
structure: Countdown in a closed space. The hammam rooms (cold, warm, hot, then door and alleys) are the chapters, and each chapter ends on a parking-meter minute-mark: 43, 24, 9, then zero and a ticket issued four minutes after expiry.
surface_question: suspense: Will Khadija catch the thin woman with the purse in the act before her meter runs out?
deep_question: When we refuse a life, do we spend the rest of ours paying every small debt on time so we never have to see that life lived by someone else?
place: A women's-day hammam in the old medina of Fès (cold, warm and hot rooms), plus the parking meter outside Bab Boujloud and the uphill alleys between them
role: Night-shift supermarket cashier who keeps a notebook of customers' uncollected one- and two-dirham debts
symbolic_object: Black flats with a gold buckle bought for a night bus to Tangier: hers, size 37, never worn and still in tissue under the bed; their twin, size 38, resoled and soft at the heels, among the wet slippers at the hammam door (secondary: gold hoop earrings bought with the shared 380-dirham tin)
story_sound: The clean 'clac' of two-dirham coins dropping into the parking meter, then the silent coin given into a palm, and at the end fingernails scraping an empty Nescafé jar
wildcard: The double (the heavy woman, Dija) is only ever seen from behind. When she finally begins to turn, Khadija's eyes, and the story's, go to the clock
ending_type: Flight and false settlement: she leaves before the face is seen, finds a 100-dirham parking ticket already under the wiper, has no coins left, folds the ticket in four
final_image: Thumb resting on her left gold hoop after folding the parking ticket
last_line: Son pouce est monté jusqu'à la boucle gauche, et il est resté là.
last_line_en: Her thumb rose to the left hoop, and it stayed there.

roll.place: A hammam in the old medina of Fès on women's day
roll.role: A supermarket cashier on the night shift
roll.object: A pair of shoes, one size too small, never worn
roll.pressure: One hour left on a parking meter
roll.wildcard: A character is only ever seen from behind
